title: Minimax Pointwise Dose-Response Estimation from a Calibrated Circular Proxy Experiment
banked_reason: D0.5: incremental tier below field floor; matched proxy frontier remains unproved.
gap_reasons: The note proves an elaborate n^(-4/7) risk upper bound and n^(-2/7) honest-length upper bound, but its lower bounds are only the generic direct-dose floors n^(-4/5) and n^(-2/5), leaving the minimax exponents unidentified.

The purported joint-proxy difficulty is not captured by the converse: the estimator uses only Z for both treatment and marked-moment deconvolution, while the lower submodel makes both proxies irrelevant.
paper_score_ceiling 5.4 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a data-only n^(-4/7) risk upper bound, an n^(-2/7) honest-length upper bound, and full-observation direct-dose lower bounds of orders n^(-4/5) and n^(-2/5), respectively. It discharged the pilot certificate but could not match the lower exponents: the abstract channel assumptions control an unweighted proxy norm, while the full likelihood requires a weighted joint-proxy norm. A matched converse or a channel-adaptive sharp rate remains a new theorem; the D0.5 review graded the proved unequal bracket incremental, below the field floor.
tldr: For one prespecified stratum and one interior continuous dose, the calibrated circular observed law identifies the conditional-ratio functional. Its equality to the causal mean is scoped by a common jointly measurable counterfactual mean version satisfying random-index mean exchangeability and continuity at the designated dose; these conditions narrow latent causal completions without changing the observed statistical nuisance class. The established statistical result is an unmatched bracket. A data-only quadratic-corrected multiscale estimator, its uniform finite-grid constrained-pilot certificate, and random-stratum count transfer give mean-squared risk at most \(C_{\mathrm{front}}(n\pi_0)^{-4/7}\) and uniformly honest connected-interval expected length at most \(C_{\mathrm{front}}(n\pi_0)^{-2/7}\). A legal binary direct-dose submodel gives all-observation lower floors \(c_{\mathrm{front}}(n\pi_0)^{-4/5}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{front}}(n\pi_0)^{-2/5}\), including at the compatible boundaries \(L=1\), \(c_p=1\), and \(C_p=1\). The exponents remain unmatched because the actual full likelihood is weighted by the generally nonconstant baseline \(T1=h_0(W-Z)\), and the frozen channel assumptions do not control the required weighted joint-proxy information.
gap: MiaoGengTchetgen2018 and Singh2020KernelUnobserved supply identification and the continuous-dose proxy framework. WuFuWangSun2024, Theorem 6.4, reports \(n^{-4/5}\) MSE for a kernel doubly robust estimator under bridge estimation, twice-continuous dose smoothness, boundedness, and a nuisance product-rate condition; HamWuCui2026DoseResponse gives debiased bridge-based inference. SchluttenhoferJohannes2020CircularQuadratic and Butucea2007QuadraticDeconvolution settle global quadratic inverse problems. None gives a primitive same-class fixed-dose upper and full-observation minimax lower bound plus a uniformly honest connected-interval length frontier for the known calibrated circular channel.
fill: The contribution begins after inherited identification: it derives a primitive known-channel \(n^{-4/7}\) upper rate with an explicit spectral-tail and projected-positivity budget, pairs it with a legal positive Bernoulli full-\((S,A,Y,Z,W)\) converse on the same class, and converts the certificate and testing mixture into a matched \(n^{-2/7}\) uniformly honest connected-interval length result.
